body: **Review record** from `review-points.md` (4 read-only Sonnet subagents (correctness, security, ticket-fit, tests briefs)): 4 auto-fixed · 9 declined and still open · 3 assumptions. Each open one is on the line it is about, or quoted below with its lines when that line is not in the diff.

comments.title: Vet tests read the session cache, not the database
comments.body:
**Auto-fixed** — Vet tests read the session cache, not the database

**Reviewer:** VisitTest is @Transactional and only one test cleared the persistence context, so create/update/clear read back the cached entity. A broken vet_id mapping or a clear that never reached the row would still pass.

**Fix:** a flushAndClear() helper runs after every write the vet tests then assert on.

<sub>raised by tests reviewer</sub>

comments.title: Unknown vetId on edit and on owner-page booking untested
comments.body:
**Auto-fixed** — Unknown vetId on edit and on owner-page booking untested

**Reviewer:** Only POST /api/visits had an unknown-vet test; PUT /api/visits/{id} and POST /owners/{o}/pets/{p}/visits could regress to a 500 unnoticed.

**Fix:** one 404 test per path.

<sub>raised by tests reviewer</sub>

comments.title: Deleting a vet with visits is untested
comments.body:
**Auto-fixed** — Deleting a vet with visits is untested

**Reviewer:** Keeping a deleted vet's visits rests on ON DELETE SET NULL in V4, and nothing exercised it; the delete could fail on the foreign key.

**Fix:** test deletes a vet through the API and reads the visit back with no vet.

<sub>raised by tests reviewer</sub>

comments.title: Chatbot list_visits omits the vet
comments.anchor: public record VisitView(int id, int petId, String petName, LocalDate date, LocalTime time, String description,
comments.body:
**Auto-fixed** — Chatbot list_visits omits the vet

**Reviewer:** The ticket says visits show their vet everywhere, yet the MCP list_visits answer had no vet field.

**Fix:** VisitView carries vetName, null when the visit has none.

<sub>raised by ticket-fit reviewer</sub>

comments.title: PUT without vetId clears the stored vet
comments.body:
**Open issue** · low · declined by the author — PUT without vetId clears the stored vet

**Why declined:** PUT replaces the whole visit, so a clear always sticks (ticket item 2); our form always sends vetId.

comments.title: Deleting a vet keeps their visits, with no vet
comments.anchor: ALTER TABLE visits ADD COLUMN vet_id INT REFERENCES vets (id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — Deleting a vet keeps their visits, with no vet

**Not taken:** refuse deleting a vet who has visits

**Why:** Ticket item 4 makes "no vet" a normal state, and before this change vet deletion always succeeded. Losing who attended is a real history loss, so a business owner could reasonably pick refusal.

comments.title: "No vet" is the wording for a visit without one
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.75 — "No vet" is the wording for a visit without one

**Not taken:** "—" or "Not assigned"

**Why:** Ticket item 4 rules out "Unknown" and blank; "No vet" says "has none" literally, and the same label serves as the combo placeholder.

comments.title: Seed gives a vet to some demo visits only
comments.anchor: INSERT INTO users (username, password, enabled) VALUES
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.65 — Seed gives a vet to some demo visits only

**Not taken:** leave every seeded visit without a vet

**Why:** The demo should show both states; ticket item 4 is about real legacy rows, not the demo dataset.
